lens: A deep per-bank sweep widened today’s catch well beyond the bulge bracket: alongside Couche-Tard’s ~$8.6B tender for Żabka (JPMorgan / Goldman) and Nscale/Anyscale (Goldman, Morgan Stanley), the boutiques were busy — Guggenheim on argenx’s ~$2.2B buy of Forte, Lazard on the Ripple Fiber/Verizon fiber deal, Perella Weinberg + Centerview on opposite sides of Repligen/BioLife (~$1.5B), and Jefferies on Domo’s $400M platform sale — a filing- and signing-heavy day that keeps secure rooms busy across every tier of the Street.

stories.headline: JPMorgan advises Couche-Tard and Goldman advises Żabka on Couche-Tard’s ~$8.6B tender offer for the Polish convenience giant
stories.why_it_matters: Alimentation Couche-Tard agreed to acquire a controlling stake in Żabka Group — the Warsaw-listed convenience-store operator — and launched a voluntary tender offer at PLN 32.00/share (~US$8.48), ~PLN 32.62B (~US$8.6B) equity value. The release names J.P. Morgan as exclusive financial adviser to Couche-Tard (buy-side, and lead arranger on the debt) and Goldman Sachs as exclusive financial adviser to Żabka (sell-side). A cross-border public tender for a listed retailer runs concentrated regulatory, financing, and confirmatory diligence toward the offer close.
stories.suggested_action: Open with JPMorgan (Couche-Tard) and Goldman (Żabka) — a ~$8.6B cross-border tender for a listed retailer runs securities-regulator, financing, and confirmatory diligence a secure room is built for.

deal_clock.event: Couche-Tard agrees to buy control of Żabka; launches PLN 32.00/share tender

stories.headline: Goldman leads and Morgan Stanley advises Nscale on its acquisition of AI-compute platform Anyscale

The release names Goldman Sachs International as lead financial adviser and Morgan Stanley as financial adviser to Nscale (buy-side); Qatalyst advised Anyscale (sell-side). An AI-infrastructure roll-up runs IP, contract, and technical diligence across two fast-scaling platforms.

stories.headline: Indices rally into month-end but advisory stocks slide a third day: S&P +0.4%, Nasdaq +0.8% while GS -3.6%, EVR -5.6%, LAZ -4.8%
stories.why_it_matters: US equities rallied Jul 31 into month-end — S&P 500 +0.4% (~7,442), Nasdaq +0.8% (~25,185), Dow +0.6% (~52,246), though the Russell 2000 slipped -0.3% — with the VIX easing to ~17.5 and WTI jumping ~3.5% to ~$85.50; the 10Y backed up to ~4.73%. But advisory names extended their drawdown for a third straight session: Goldman -3.6%, Evercore -5.6%, Lazard -4.8%, Jefferies -1.9%, Morgan Stanley -1.6% (Moelis and PJT bucked the trend, +1.6% / +0.2%). A weak advisory tape against a firm market doesn’t slow signed processes — it sharpens the case for certainty of execution.
stories.suggested_action: Frame outreach around execution certainty — with the advisory complex under pressure into August but signings steady, clients want their live processes to stay on schedule; room readiness protects the timeline.

items.why_unverified: Bloomberg-originated reporting; Alkami has not confirmed the letter, the buyer interest, or any process. Buyer identities and any adviser are unknown. (Distinct from the Fiserv/JANA situation — same activist, different target.)

items.lead: Leonardo said it remains in non-binding talks with Germany’s Rheinmetall over selling part of Iveco Defence Vehicles — a “gentlemen’s agreement, but nothing formally binding” — and has fielded enquiries from other interested parties, framing a sale as one of several options.
items.why_unverified: Leonardo acknowledges the talks (so not pure rumor), but there is no binding agreement, no price, and no chosen buyer; management calls a sale just one option among several. No adviser named.

items.company: Virgin Media O2 (owners Telefónica / Liberty Global)
items.lead: Per an FT report, VMO2’s shareholders are weighing steps to address a ~£22bn debt pile after a sharp bond sell-off — options cited include cutting the ~£200M dividend, headcount reductions, and lower capex, the kind of balance-sheet pressure that often precedes asset disposals.
items.why_unverified: Anonymous-sourced FT report; no confirmation from VMO2, Telefónica, or Liberty Global. The options discussed are restructuring/balance-sheet moves, not yet an outright asset sale, and no adviser is named.

items.company: GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) — Patient Care Solutions
items.lead: On its Q2 call, CEO Peter Arduini confirmed a formal review of strategic options for the Patient Care Solutions segment (patient-monitoring, anesthesia delivery) — explicitly including “a sale and other value-enhancing transactions.” Segment Q2 revenue was $675M, down 13.3%.
items.why_unverified: COMPANY-CONFIRMED that a review is underway — but whether it sells, at what price, to whom, with which adviser, and on what timeline are all unconfirmed. Actionable as a potential carve-out mandate, not a rumored deal.

items.lead: Bloomberg reports Deutsche Lufthansa and Air France-KLM submitted binding offers for a stake as Portugal sells up to 49.9% of flag carrier TAP (5% reserved for employees) — one of Europe’s last mid-sized carriers still on the market.
items.why_unverified: A live government privatization with binding bids reportedly in — more “confirmed live process” than rumor — but bid amounts, the winner, and timeline are unconfirmed, and reporting is anonymous-sourced. No adviser named.
